ranked_findings.title: Potassium salt substitute with RAAS inhibitor or MRA
ranked_findings.summary: Potassium salt substitute logged on 5 day(s) between 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-02 while Lisinopril and Spironolactone are active; severity raised to high because an MRA is active and potassium 5.6 mEq/L is at or above 5 (DEC-05).
ranked_findings.patient_question: I use a salt substitute. Is it safe with my heart medicines?
ranked_findings.clinician_note: Most salt substitutes contain potassium chloride.

thresholds_used.parameter: R07 escalation: potassium rise vs previous result

ranked_findings.title: High potassium on an MRA
ranked_findings.summary: Potassium was 5.6 mEq/L on 2026-09-30 while Spironolactone (MRA) is active; the alert level is 5.5 mEq/L or higher.
ranked_findings.patient_question: My potassium was 5.6 mEq/L. Should my Spironolactone be adjusted?
ranked_findings.clinician_note: Guideline addresses MRA continuation when potassium stays above the threshold; review MRA therapy.

ranked_findings.title: Rapid weight gain

ranked_findings.patient_question: My weight went up 2.5 kg in 5 days. Should I contact my care team?

ranked_findings.title: Missed doses

ranked_findings.clinician_note: Reason guides solution (cost, side effects, diuretic timing).
